mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month consecutive decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) signals industrial slowdown, reducing corporate production capacity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output decline below its 3-month moving average (INDPRO < 3-month MA) indicates industrial contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals inflationary pressure that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate increases (UNRATE rising) and employment declines (PAYEMS falling) signal labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending power and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annualized growth rate exceeding 3%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced growth momentum and profit-taking.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate > 3% annualized.
